messages:
emma: Heads-up — I ran the new reranker (royal-rank-v1) through the staging evals with mixed-layer quant (4bit lower layers, 8bit top layers). Results look...weird. NDCG@10 up on websearch-sample but MRR@5 drops on short queries.
raj: Can you paste the metric table?
emma: quick snapshot: NDCG@10 +1.8% overall, MRR@5 -4.2% on short-queries slice, long-doc slice unchanged. Full table in gdrive (link) but here's the head: `ndcg10: 0.412 -> 0.419`, `mrr5_short: 0.273 -> 0.262`.
sophie: interesting. Did you change tokenization or candidate ordering during inference? even small reorders can hit MRR.
emma: no intentional changes in ordering. Same sampling seed. But I did try two input formatting variants: (A) docs joined with single space, (B) docs joined with newline+<sep>. A seemed to correlate with the MRR dip.
mike: newline vs space affecting attention patterns — plausible, esp with quantization altering low-level activations. We saw similar brittle behavior with other small models.
raj: can we run ablation: royal-rank-v1 quantized + format A vs B, and the fp32 baseline with A vs B? Need 2x2 to disentangle. Also include candidate shuffling probe (random 5% reorder) to see sensitivity.
nora: I kicked off the 2x2 job on staging cluster (job id rk-5178). ETA ~45m. Also doing a tokenization parity check against prod tokenizer binary.
deploy-bot: Model royal-rank-v1 (quant-mixed) deployed to staging for evaluation by @nora — job rk-5178 started.
emma: hypothesis: mixed-layer quant shifts top-k logits distribution for short queries where top answers are close; that hurts MRR but may improve overall ndcg by better tail ordering. If true, calibration/rescaling of output logits or temperature per-slice might recover MRR.
sophie: let's also run calibration sweep: scale factors [0.95, 1.0, 1.05] and softmax temp [0.9, 1.0, 1.1] on staging inference pipeline. Keep batch size constant.
mike: add an eval on LegalKB subset and on the curated 'few-shot-paraphrase' holdout to ensure not regressing on niche domains.
raj: re: datasets — can we confirm the websearch-sample candidate pool size? If candidate pool changed (100 -> 200) ndcg could move independently.
emma: confirmed pool still 100. I also checked the KV-cache alignment — no mismatches.
nora: RK job finished. Quick notes: format B (newline) + mixed quant gives best ndcg; format A + mixed quant gives the MRR dip. fp32 baseline unaffected by format. Uploading run artifacts to s3://redwood-staging/rk-5178.
emma: thanks — can you share the conf matrix? I want to run pairwise significance (bootstrap) on short-query MRR.
nora: uploaded stats.json and per-query deltas. Link in thread.
raj: next steps: 1) bootstrapped CI for MRR difference; 2) calibration sweep; 3) candidate-order sensitivity probe; 4) if still bad, try per-layer hybrid: keep middle layers in fp16 and low bits only on attention projections.
sophie: capture this as a checklist in the reranker bringup doc so PMs/CS can see the risk.
emma: agreed. I'll start the calibration sweep now and keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
